clue.text: Nursery slope climbers

parts.note: a nursery rhyme pair who went up the hill to fetch a pail of water, read as skiers on a beginners' slope

explanation.surface: Novice skiers labouring up the gentle practice run.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'nursery slope' is a gentle ski run for beginners, but here 'Nursery' points to a nursery rhyme and 'slope' to its hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's boy and girl climb a hill for water, so they are the best-known climbers in children's verse.

clue.text: Meet Mr Heath and be articulate

parts.note: to meet is to join, as two roads do
Edward Heath, British Prime Minister 1970-74, was known as Ted

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet the former Prime Minister and speak well.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was a British Conservative Prime Minister. 'Articulate' here is the adjective for having joints, not the verb for speaking clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulate limb or stalk is one built in segments linked by joints.

clue.text: But for whom Barkis would not have been willing

definitions.text: But for whom Barkis would not have been willing

parts.words: But for whom Barkis would not have been willing
parts.note: Barkis, the carrier in David Copperfield, sends the message 'Barkis is willin''; without his author he would never have said it

explanation.surface: A character's willingness owed entirely to one person.
explanation.walkthrough: Barkis is the carrier in David Copperfield who proposes to Peggotty with 'Barkis is willin''. The person without whom he would not exist, or be willing, is his creator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian novelist wrote David Copperfield and so created Barkis and his famous catchphrase.

clue.text: Wily monarch beheading Scotsman.

indicators.note: beheading cuts the front off the word monarch, here the stretch the Scotsman supplies

parts.note: 'mon' is the stock Scots form of address 'man', as in 'hoots mon'

explanation.surface: A cunning king decapitates a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheading' removes MON, the crossword's Scotsman, from the front of MONARCH, leaving ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means knowingly sly or roguish, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: Wanted a knighthood, indeed

indicators.note: the word indeed splits as in plus deed, so in tells us to put the title inside

parts.note: taken as written
a knighthood brings the title Sir

explanation.surface: Someone who really did want to be knighted.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'indeed' must be read as two words, 'in deed', which is how the knight's title gets placed: a split word solvers often miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something desired is longed for, the past participle matching the clue's verb form.

clue.text: See 1
An Indian religion is in turn in a preserve

indicators.note: the second in tells us the swapped pair of words sits inside the preserve

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
the words is and in, taken in turn the other way round, read in followed by is

explanation.surface: A remark that a faith belongs, for a while, in a protected area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' looks like 'one after another' but swaps the order of the two little words, and the second 'in' places them inside the preserve. Jainism is the faith founded by Mahavira.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient faith of the Jains, founded by Mahavira, is one of India's native religions.

clue.text: One using oils in her make-up

indicators.note: her make-up suggests the composition of the letters, so oils is rearranged into a name

explanation.surface: A woman who wears oil-based cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but signals the letters of OILS made up again into a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'One ... her' points to a woman, and the name is one such woman's name.

clue.text: Ancient country city has C transformed

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of city has are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An old nation whose city underwent a change.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging CITY HAS gives the land of the Scythians, a nomadic people north of the Black Sea in antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient region on the Eurasian steppe was home to the horse-riding Scythians.

clue.text: Trust a Job's comforter to do so

definitions.text: Trust a Job's comforter to do so

parts.words: Trust a Job's comforter to do so
parts.note: a Job's comforter makes misery worse while pretending to console, so one can be relied on to exaggerate suffering

explanation.surface: A wry remark about a friend who only makes things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: Job's comforters, in the Book of Job, blamed him for his own misfortunes; the phrase now means someone whose sympathy deepens the distress.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exaggerate a painful situation, exactly what a false comforter does.

clue.text: Unapproachable state

parts.note: the condition of being impossible to reach or approach, read also as if naming a country

explanation.surface: A remote country nobody can reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unapproachable is being impossible to get to, the quality the long noun names.

clue.text: Up to work with a plough

explanation.surface: A farmer working the land right up to a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means until or up to a time; as a verb it means cultivate soil by ploughing.

clue.text: Profit right in a measure

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for right goes inside the word for profit

parts.note: a profit is a gain

explanation.surface: Making money correctly in a set quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside GAIN. The definition is a unit of weight, the smallest in the old British system.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of weight, about 65 milligrams, was once based on a single seed of wheat.

clue.text: Rachel's sister in a race a mile ahead

indicators.note: in signals that the name sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A Biblical sister running a race and leading by a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'miLE AHead'. In Genesis Jacob worked seven years for Rachel but was first given her elder sister.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Laban's elder daughter married Jacob before her sister Rachel did.

clue.text: Close to one's fingertips

parts.note: within easy reach, literally near the hand

explanation.surface: Something within easy reach.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means conveniently near, and it contains the hand the fingertips belong to.

clue.text: Given a pleased-to see-you look

parts.note: stared at with obvious admiring or amorous interest

explanation.surface: Being looked at by someone visibly glad of your company.
explanation.definitionFit: To be eyed with leering interest is to be the target of a lingering admiring stare.

clue.text: Father inherently brilliant but a coward

indicators.note: inherently means within, so the brilliant word lies inside the father's word

parts.note: dad is a familiar word for father
a star is someone brilliant at what they do

explanation.surface: A dad who is innately gifted yet lacks courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inherently' looks like it describes the father's talent, but it signals that one piece sits inside the other. Dastard is an archaic word for a sneaking coward.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a contemptible coward who acts in a sneaky, cruel way.

clue.text: Hue of a harassed magnate

indicators.note: harassed means stressed and disordered, so the letters of magnate are jumbled

explanation.surface: The colour of a stressed business tycoon's face.
explanation.definitionFit: The purplish-red dye is a colour, named after a battle of 1859.

clue.text: Pirate captain observed around in peak form

indicators.note: around tells us the word for observed wraps round the pirate

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, to observe
Captain William Kidd was a notorious 17th-century pirate

explanation.surface: A buccaneer watched as he was seen at his best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the containment signal. The answer is a mountain in England's Lake District; 'in peak form' looks like 'at one's best'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain near Keswick is one of the highest summits in England's Lake District.

clue.text: Sounder dwelling housing 3, to be precise

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the pig home holds the answer to the third clue

parts.note: a sounder is a herd of wild pigs, and a pig's home is a sty
the answer to 3-down, meaning wily or knowing

explanation.surface: A home for swine that contains the third answer, put exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounder' is not a comparative of sound: it is the collective noun for a herd of swine, whose dwelling is a STY. It houses the answer to 3-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stiffly formal and fussy, as if stiffened like a collar, is overly precise.

clue.text: Tired of keeping to the beaten track?

definitions.text: Tired of keeping to the beaten track?

parts.words: Tired of keeping to the beaten track?
parts.note: read literally, worn out from travelling along a road; the phrase looks like bored of conventional routes

explanation.surface: Someone bored with conventional ways of doing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired of' suggests boredom, but it means exhausted by the journey: worn down by the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally weary from travel, worn by the way one has walked.

clue.text: Buckinghamshire town that brings a hush in Cheam

indicators.note: in places the call for quiet inside the Surrey place name

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the sound made to call for hush

explanation.surface: A town whose name quietens down a Surrey suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheam is a suburb in south London; 'in' is the containment signal. Chesham is a town in the Chiltern hills, at the end of a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: The market town in the Chilterns lies in the county of Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: Roman who was stupid to us C

parts.note: crass means grossly stupid or insensitive
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman insulting our intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Licinius Crassus was the wealthy Roman who formed the First Triumvirate with Caesar and Pompey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman general and plutocrat was a member of the First Triumvirate.

clue.text: Pacific revolutionary girl

parts.note: pacific means peaceable and gentle, which is mild
a red is a revolutionary socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A peaceable young woman with radical politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' looks like the ocean but is the adjective meaning gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so the name of a girl.

clue.text: Little birds a predator gull turns on.

indicators.note: turns means the predatory gull's name is read backwards

parts.note: the skua is a large seabird that robs and preys on other birds

explanation.surface: Small birds being attacked by a predatory gull.
explanation.walkthrough: SKUA read backwards gives the answer. 'turns on' looks like 'attacks'.
explanation.definitionFit: The diving seabirds include the little auk and the puffin.

clue.text: … and a hymn composed for another

indicators.note: composed means arranged anew, so the letters of a hymn are reordered

explanation.surface: A hymn written for a different occasion, continuing the last clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this clue to 21-across, so 'another' means another bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Following the birds of the previous clue, it is another bird, a talking starling from Asia.

clue.text: Highlander with the wind up, one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a gale is a wind risen to great strength

explanation.surface: A Scottish Highlander who is frightened, someone says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the wind up' looks like 'scared', but a GALE is wind that has got up.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gaelic-speaking Scot, typically from the Highlands.

clue.text: Point to a lower form of craft

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
a cow lows, so it is a lower

explanation.surface: Pointing someone to a lesser kind of vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not the comparative of low: it means one that lows, a COW.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed boat used for carrying cargo.

clue.text: A sticky outer island

indicators.note: outer tells us the sticky substance goes outside the letter A

parts.note: gum is a sticky substance

explanation.surface: An adhesive coating on the outside of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: GUM goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific island is a US territory in the Marianas.

clue.text: It's not by any chance funny

definitions.text: It's not by any chance funny

parts.words: It's not by any chance funny
parts.note: comedy that is deliberate, not accidental

explanation.surface: A question whether something might be amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not by any chance funny' looks like a doubting question, but it means funny not by chance: intentionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit that knows it is being witty, deliberate rather than accidental comedy.

clue.text: He would owe nothing initially

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word nothing

explanation.surface: A man who would be in debt for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: OWE plus N, the first letter of 'nothing', gives a Welsh man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A male name, so a fair stand-in for the pronoun.

clue.text: Language from which odes may be translated

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters of odes may are rearranged

explanation.surface: A language that poems might be rendered from.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Samoyedic language family of Siberia; it is also a dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyedic languages are spoken by Siberian peoples such as the Nenets.
